name: paired-model-inventory-plan-stress-test
assumptions: Timestral 209M LoRA, the trained LSTM, and Google TimesFM 3.0 head-tuned forecasts share exactly 2,693 products and all 28 target dates.
The October 5-November 1, 2011 period was previously reused in exploratory/model evaluation work and is descriptive, not a pristine blind benchmark.
Each model plan uses the same order-up-to formula: forecast expected demand over sampled lead time plus seven review days, with the same 20% safety-stock fraction.
Demand starts from the same observed October 5-November 1 recorded-sales path for every model and is scaled by a portfolio-wide multiplier in each scenario.

Demand multiplier is 1.0, 1.25, or 1.5 with probabilities 70%, 20%, and 10%; supplier delay is 0, 2, 5, or 10 days with probabilities 70%, 20%, 8%, and 2%; starting stock loss is 0%, 10%, 25%, or 50% with probabilities 70%, 15%, 10%, and 5%.
All model plans share the same synthetic starting stock, incoming orders, lead times, demand paths, delivery delays, stock losses, and costs.
Recorded sales do not reveal demand lost during stockouts. Holding, order placement, and shortage costs are illustrative; purchase cost is excluded.
